data.description: Residual from C11-209 (PR #433, shipped in 0.65.1). C11-209 fixed the never-loaded WKWebView wedge (fail-fast in 0.14s), made download.wait resolve early, and capped timeout_ms at 120s. What it deliberately did NOT do: move browser.* out of v2MainSync into socketWorkerV2Methods, because those handlers are @MainActor-isolated (production stack: MainActor.assumeIsolated directly above v2BrowserWait). Measured consequence on the validated tagged build: on a LOADED page with an unmet 20s wait, 'c11 tree' stalled 10.0s while 'c11 ping' answered in 0.142s, i.e. every main-marshalled socket command (tree, read-screen, focus, send) still waits out any in-flight browser wait, now bounded at 120s instead of unbounded. Work: make the browser wait/eval family complete asynchronously (or run its await off-main with only the WebKit calls hopped to main), keep the C11-209 tests and harness (tools/await-wedge-repro) as the regression oracle, and re-run the positive-control probe: 'c11 tree' must answer in well under 1s during a 20s unmet browser wait on a loaded page. Read docs/c11-browser-await-main-wedge.md first.
data.title: Move browser.* socket handlers off the main thread so a legitimate wait never stalls main-marshalled commands

data.body:
# C11-217 implementation plan

## Scope and dispatch

- Move `browser.eval`, `browser.wait`, and `browser.download.wait` into
  `TerminalController.socketWorkerV2Methods` and add explicit worker-dispatch
  cases. These are the browser wait/eval endpoints that can hold a caller for a
  caller-sized timeout. Navigation, focus, tab/workspace, selector-action,
  snapshot, cookie, screenshot, state, and unsupported browser handlers remain
  main-bound for this ticket: they touch AppKit/WebKit/model state synchronously
  and a broad rewrite would be unrelated to the acceptance seam.
- Preserve the existing main-actor `v2DispatchBrowser` route as the fallback
  implementation shape, but make the three moved methods `nonisolated` and
  give them explicit worker phases. The worker path will refresh handle refs on
  main before resolving IDs, matching the work already done by the existing
  `surface.*` worker handlers.

## Browser phases

1. A short `Task { @MainActor }` resolves `TabManager`/workspace/surface,
   checks the C11-209 `hasIssuedLoad` guard for eval/wait, snapshots the current
   frame selector, and builds the response envelope while `v2Ref` and model
   state are safely on main. It returns only the target `WKWebView`, immutable
   IDs/envelope, and the frame-selector snapshot to the worker.
2. The worker builds the existing JS wrapper from that frame-selector snapshot
   and waits with the semaphore branch of `v2AwaitCallback`. The WebKit call is
   submitted with `DispatchQueue.main.async` and therefore starts on main, but
   the worker—not a `v2MainSync` block—waits for its completion. The completion
   signals the worker directly; no nested `CFRunLoopRunInMode` is used.
3. The worker decodes the result and returns the already-built envelope. A
   `browser.wait` keeps its existing JS condition/selector semantics and the
   existing 1-second Swift grace; a loaded-page eval keeps its result and
   isolated-world retry behavior.

`v2RunJavaScript` and `v2RunBrowserJavaScript` will share their pure wrapper /
decode helpers with a new off-main runner, so the main-bound call sites retain
their behavior without reading actor state from the worker. The off-main await
will use a lock/once gate: a timeout marks the request cancelled, prevents a
queued main invocation from starting, and ignores any late WebKit completion.
The existing monotonic timeout remains authoritative.

## Download and terminal waits

- `browser.download.wait` will resolve/validate its browser surface in the
  main phase, then run `DownloadPathWatcher` and the notification wait on the
  worker. The C11-222 invariants remain unchanged: watcher state is serial-
  queue-confined, descriptors close only from source cancel handlers,
  `teardown()` runs on every path, and the waiter observer is removed after
  success or timeout. An observed event is popped from the controller's queue
  by a short main-actor phase so the queue remains the single source of truth.
- Sweep the legacy `waitForTerminalSurface` hazard by routing the v1 `send`,
  `send_key`, `send_surface`, and `send_key_surface` commands through worker
  phases that use the existing `waitForTerminalSurfaceOffMain` helper, then
  re-hop to main only to revalidate the pointer and inject input. This removes
  the legacy main-queue notification wait from socket-reachable paths while
  preserving the v1 response/error behavior. Do not change unrelated terminal
  commands.

## Tests and validation

- Add behavioral policy/await coverage for the three worker browser methods,
  timeout cancellation/late completion, and concurrent independent waits where
  a host-free seam can exercise it; keep C11-209 pump and C11-222 watcher tests.
- Build only through the lock-wrapped tagged reload/automation scripts. The
  tagged socket probe will record the pre-change loaded-page baseline (C11-209
  measured `tree` at 10.0 s during a 20 s wait), then verify `tree` is under 1
  s during an unmet 20 s wait, `no_document` remains fast, the 120 s cap,
  loaded eval, early download completion, and two simultaneous waits.
- Do not run local `xcodebuild test`, launch an untagged app, modify Ghostty or
  `.lattice/`, merge, deploy, or claim browser proof from source/tests alone.

# C11-217 handoff

## Change

PR #442: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/442

Commit: `df03b426dbd7ea23409667686e3dabe3eb4d31f8`

- `browser.eval`, `browser.wait`, and `browser.download.wait` now use the socket-worker policy.
- Main actor work is limited to resolving refs, the workspace/panel, document guard, selector, frame, and response envelope. The worker owns the potentially long wait; each WebKit invocation is submitted with `DispatchQueue.main.async`, with no nested main-run-loop pump.
- The download path continues to use the C11-222 private-queue watcher and teardown/descriptor ownership. Event queue append/pop uses the main-actor bridge.
- Legacy `send`, `send_key`, `send_surface`, and `send_key_surface` now resolve their terminal panel on main, wait with `waitForTerminalSurfaceOffMain`, then revalidate and inject on main.
- Other `browser.*` handlers remain main-bound.

## Local build and tagged runtime evidence

Build command:

    ./scripts/with-build-lock.sh xcodebuild -project GhosttyTabs.xcodeproj -scheme c11-logic -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO

Result: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`.

Tagged build/launch:

    C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh ./scripts/reload.sh --tag c11-217-browser-offmain

Socket: `/tmp/c11-debug-c11-217-browser-offmain.sock`

- C11-209 before benchmark: the historical main-held browser stall/CLI give-up was 10.0s.
- On the loaded tagged page, `browser eval '1 + 1'` returned `2` in `0.15s`.
- A fresh never-loaded browser surface returned `no_document` from eval in `0.14s`.
- During an unmet 20s `browser wait` (`#c11-never-exists`), tagged `tree --no-layout` returned in `0.14s`; the wait itself ran to `20.15s` before timing out.
- Two waits on separate loaded browser surfaces, started concurrently and released by separate DOM mutations, both returned `waited: true` (`10.28s` and `6.30s`).
- A download path wait resolved when a 1-byte fixture appeared, in `4.24s` against a 10s timeout.

## CI

`gh pr checks 442 --repo Stage-11-Agentics/c11` completed successfully. Passing checks: build, build-ghosttykit, compat-tests (macos-15, 30, true, false), drawbridge-judge, drawbridge-gate, drawbridge-review, drawbridge-notify, remote-daemon-tests, web-typecheck, and workflow-guard-tests. `drawbridge-merge` was skipped by the workflow.

Local XCTest actions were deliberately not run per the brief; CI is the test gate.

## Boundaries

No merge, deployment, untagged app launch, or unrelated browser-handler changes. No skill source changed, so no installed-skill sync is required.

After merge: remove the tagged QA app/DerivedData if still present; no runtime deployment step is required for this ticket.

PASS. PR #442 squash-merged. browser.eval, browser.wait and browser.download.wait now run under the socket-worker policy: a short main-actor phase resolves refs, the no_document guard, selector and frame, then the per-connection worker owns the wait while each WebKit call hops to main via DispatchQueue.main.async under a lock-guarded begin/complete/cancel gate, so a timeout suppresses a not-yet-started call and drops a late completion; no nested run-loop pump. Legacy send/send_key/send_surface/send_key_surface resolve on main, wait with waitForTerminalSurfaceOffMain, and re-hop to inject, closing the third instance. Other browser.* handlers stay main-bound. Delegator's tagged runtime probe: tree answered in 0.14 s during a 20 s unmet wait (10.0 s stall before), eval 0.15 s, no_document 0.14 s, two concurrent waits on separate surfaces released independently, download wait resolved early. CI green including the policy test. Residual: the remaining browser.* handlers still marshal to main for their synchronous work, by design.
